outcome: maternal stress (total PSS: NICU scores and subscales: Sights and Sounds, Infant Appearance and Behavior, Parental Role Alteration)
cohort: The study included 247 mothers of preterm infants admitted to the NICU, categorized into two groups based on infant gestational age (<=32 weeks and >32 weeks).
finding: Mothers of infants with gestational age <=32 weeks experienced higher NICU-related stress and worry, with specific factors such as infant medical conditions, maternal demographics, and birth characteristics influencing stress levels differently across gestational age groups.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with higher stress and worry in mothers of extremely/very preterm infants, whereas vaginal delivery was linked to higher stress in mothers of moderate/late preterm neonates.
cross-section timing: During the infant's Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) stay
